beats.say: In 264 BC Carthage slipped a stealth fleet from Lilybaeum past Roman patrols under moon tonight.
Roman commander Gaius Duilius anchored his quinqueremes near Sicily, trusting traditional naval dominance over.
Carthaginian sailors set fire to Roman oars, turning the calm sea into a blazing trap.
Chaos forced Rome to invent the corvus boarding bridge, forever changing naval combat tactics dramatically.
The raid seized the grain convoy from Enna, starving Roman legions stationed on Sicily soon.
Roman Senate responded by creating the first praetors with explicit naval command authority for the.
Carthage's bold strike delayed the Roman African invasion by two years, buying crucial defensive time.
Later that year Rome won at Mylae, proving the corvus could turn disaster into victory.
Traditional histories claim Carthage never threatened Rome's navy; this night raid shatters that myth completely.
